shloka_text: नारायणगिरिं ते तु गर्जन्तो राक्षसाम्बुदाः । ववर्षुः शरवर्षेण वर्षेणेवाद्रिमम्बुदाः ।। 7.7.1 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇagiriṃ te tu garjanto rākṣasāmbudāḥ | vavarṣuḥ śaravarṣeṇa varṣeṇevādrimambudāḥ || 7.7.1 ||
translation: नारायणगिरिं towards the mountain Narayana, ते those, तु indeed, गर्जन्तः roaring, राक्षसाम्बुदाः the demon-clouds, ववर्षुः showered, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षेण with rain, इव like, अद्रिम् upon a mountain, अम्बुदाः clouds,
explanation: Those roaring demon-clouds, like actual clouds showering rain upon a mountain, indeed showered a rain of arrows upon the mountain-like Narayana (Vishnu/Rama).
comments: The great battle between Vishnu and the rakshasa host -- withstanding their showers of arrows, Vishnu blows his conch Panchajanya, slays them by thousands and routs their army toward Lanka -- Sumali is whirled from the field by his maddened horses -- Mali fights on, striking Garuda with his mace, until the enraged Vishnu severs Mali's head with his discus -- the gods rejoice, and Sumali and Malyavan flee back to Lanka.

shloka_text: श्यामावदातस्तैर्विष्णुर्नीलैर्नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः । वृतो ऽञ्जनगिरीवासीत् वर्षमाणैः पयोधरैः ।। 7.7.2 ।।
transliteration: śyāmāvadātastairviṣṇurnīlairnaktañcarottamaiḥ | vṛto 'ñjanagirīvāsīt varṣamāṇaiḥ payodharaiḥ || 7.7.2 ||
translation: श्यामावदातः dark-complexioned and radiant, तैः by them, विष्णुः Vishnu, नीलैः by the blue ones, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः by the best of night-wanderers, वृतः surrounded, अञ्जनगिरीवासीत् became like a mountain of collyrium, वर्षमाणैः showering, पयोधरैः by clouds,
explanation: The dark-complexioned and radiant Vishnu, surrounded by those blue, best of night-wanderers, became like a collyrium mountain being showered upon by clouds.

shloka_text: शलभा इव केदारं मशका इव पर्वतम् । यथामृतघटं दंशा मकरा इव चार्णवम् ।। 7.7.3 ।।
transliteration: śalabhā iva kedāraṃ maśakā iva parvatam | yathāmṛtaghaṭaṃ daṃśā makarā iva cārṇavam || 7.7.3 ||
translation: शलभाः locusts, इव like, केदारम् a field, मशकाः mosquitoes, इव like, पर्वतम् a mountain, यथा just as, अमृतघटम् a pot of nectar, दंशाः flies, मकराः crocodiles, इव like, च and, अर्णवम् the ocean,
explanation: Just as locusts swarm a field, mosquitoes a mountain, flies a pot of nectar, and crocodiles the ocean, so too did the arrows approach Hari.

shloka_text: तथा रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ता वज्रानिलमनोजवाः । हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोका इव विपर्यये ।। 7.7.4 ।।
transliteration: tathā rakṣodhanurmuktā vajrānilamanojavāḥ | hariṃ viśanti sma śarā lokā iva viparyaye || 7.7.4 ||
translation: तथा similarly, रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ताः released from the bows of demons, वज्रानिलमनोजवाः having the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, हरिम् into Hari, विशन्ति स्म entered, शराः arrows, लोकाः worlds, इव like, विपर्यये at the time of dissolution,
explanation: Similarly, arrows released from the bows of demons, possessing the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, entered Hari, just as all beings merge into the supreme at the time of cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैः स्यन्दनगता गजैश्च गजपृष्ठगाः । अश्वारोहास्तथाश्वैश्च पादाताश्चाम्बरे स्थिताः ।। 7.7.5 ।।
transliteration: syandanaiḥ syandanagatā gajaiśca gajapṛṣṭhagāḥ | aśvārohāstathāśvaiśca pādātāścāmbare sthitāḥ || 7.7.5 ||
translation: स्यन्दनैः with chariots, स्यन्दनगताः those who went in chariots, गजैः with elephants, च and, गजपृष्ठगाः those who went on elephant-backs, अश्वारोहाः horse-riders, तथा similarly, अश्वैः with horses, च and, पादाताः foot-soldiers, च and, अम्बरे in the sky, स्थिताः standing,
explanation: Those who rode in chariots, those on elephant-backs, horse-riders with their horses, and foot-soldiers, all were positioned in the sky.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रा गिरिनिभाः शरैः शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः । निरुछ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायामा इव द्विजम् ।। 7.7.6 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasendrā girinibhāḥ śaraiḥ śaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ | niruchvāsaṃ hariṃ cakruḥ prāṇāyāmā iva dvijam || 7.7.6 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द्राः demon lords, गिरिनिभाः mountain-like, शरैः with arrows, शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः with spears, lances, and javelins, निरुछ्वासं breathless, हरिं Hari, चक्रुः made, प्राणायामाः breath control exercises, इव like, द्विजम् a brahmin.
explanation: The mountain-like demon lords, using arrows, spears, lances, and javelins, rendered Hari breathless, just as breath control exercises make a brahmin breathless.

shloka_text: निशाचरैस्ताड्यमानो मीनैरिव महोदधिः । शार्ङ्गमायम्य दुर्धर्षो राक्षसेभ्यो ऽसृजच्छरान् ।। 7.7.7 ।।
transliteration: niśācaraistāḍyamāno mīnairiva mahodadhiḥ | śārṅgamāyamya durdharṣo rākṣasebhyo 'sṛjaccharān || 7.7.7 ||
translation: निशाचरैः by night-wanderers, ताड्यमानो being struck, मीनैरिव like by fish, महोदधिः the great ocean, शार्ङ्गम् the Sharnga bow, आयम्य having drawn, दुर्धर्षो the unconquerable one, राक्षसेभ्यो at the demons, असृजत् released, शरान् arrows.
explanation: Being tormented by the night-wanderers like the great ocean by fish, the unconquerable one drew his Sharnga bow and discharged arrows at the demons.

shloka_text: शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्वज्रवक्त्रैर्मनोजवैः । चिच्छेद विष्णुर्निशितैः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.8 ।।
transliteration: śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭairvajravaktrairmanojavaiḥ | ciccheda viṣṇurniśitaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ || 7.7.8 ||
translation: शरैः with arrows, पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः fully drawn and released, वज्रवक्त्रैः having thunderbolt-like points, मनोजवैः swift as thought, चिच्छेद cut, विष्णुः Vishnu, निशितैः sharp, शतशो by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: With sharp arrows, fully drawn and released, having thunderbolt-like points and swift as thought, Vishnu cut them down by hundreds and then by thousands.

shloka_text: विद्राव्य शरवर्षेण वर्षा वायुरिवोत्थितम् । पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्खं प्रदध्मौ पुरुषोत्तमः ।। 7.7.9 ।।
transliteration: vidrāvya śaravarṣeṇa varṣā vāyurivotthitam | pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhaṃ pradadhmau puruṣottamaḥ || 7.7.9 ||
translation: विद्राव्य having dispersed, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षा rain, वायुः wind, इव like, उत्थितम् risen, पाञ्चजन्यं the Panchajanya, महाशङ्खं the great conch, प्रदध्मौ blew, पुरुषोत्तमः the best among men.
explanation: Having dispersed the rain of arrows with his own arrows, just as wind disperses rain, the best among men blew his great conch, Panchajanya.

shloka_text: सो ऽम्बुजो हरिणा ध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट् । ररास भीमनिर्हादस्त्रैलोक्यं व्यथयन्निव ।। 7.7.10 ।।
transliteration: so 'mbujo hariṇā dhmātaḥ sarvaprāṇena śaṅkharāṭ | rarāsa bhīmanirhādastrailokyaṃ vyathayanniva || 7.7.10 ||
translation: सः that, अम्बुजः water-born (conch), हरिणा by Hari, ध्मातः blown, सर्वप्राणेन with all his might, शङ्खराट् the king of conches, ररास roared, भीमनिर्हादः with a terrible roar, त्रैलोक्यं the three worlds, व्यथयन् distressing, इव as if.
explanation: That water-born king of conches, blown by Hari with all his might, roared with a terrible sound, as if terrifying the three worlds.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवः सो ऽथ त्रासयामास राक्षसान् । मृगराज इवारण्ये समदानिव कुञ्जरान् ।। 7.7.11 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkharājaravaḥ so 'tha trāsayāmāsa rākṣasān | mṛgarāja ivāraṇye samadāniva kuñjarān || 7.7.11 ||
translation: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, सः that, अथ then, त्रासयामास terrified, राक्षसान् the Rākṣasas, मृगराजः a lion, इव like, अरण्ये in the forest, समदान् maddened, इव like, कुञ्जरान् elephants.
explanation: Then, the sound of the king of conches terrified the Rākṣasas, just as a lion in the forest frightens maddened elephants.

shloka_text: न शेकुरश्वाः संस्थातुं विमदाः कुञ्जराभवन् । स्यन्दनेभ्यश्च्युता वीराः शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः ।। 7.7.12 ।।
transliteration: na śekuraśvāḥ saṃsthātuṃ vimadāḥ kuñjarābhavan | syandanebhyaścyutā vīrāḥ śaṅkharāvitadurbalāḥ || 7.7.12 ||
translation: न not, शेकुः were able, अश्वाः horses, संस्थातुम् to stand still, विमदाः bereft of ichor/strength, कुञ्जराः elephants, अभवन् became, स्यन्दनेभ्यः from their chariots, च्युताः fallen, वीराः warriors, शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः weakened by the conch's sound.
explanation: The horses were unable to stand still, the elephants lost their ichor and strength, and warriors, weakened by the conch's sound, fell from their chariots.

shloka_text: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ता वज्रतुल्याननाः शराः । विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम् ।। 7.7.13 ।।
transliteration: śārṅgacāpavinirmuktā vajratulyānanāḥ śarāḥ | vidārya tāni rakṣāṃsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim || 7.7.13 ||
translation: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, वज्रतुल्याननाः having points like a thunderbolt, शराः arrows, विदार्य tearing apart, तानि those, रक्षांसि Rākṣasas, सुपुङ्खाः with good feathers, विविशुः entered, क्षितिम् the earth.
explanation: Arrows released from the Śārṅga bow, with points like thunderbolts, tore through those Rākṣasas and, with their well-feathered shafts, penetrated the earth.

shloka_text: भिद्यमानाः शरैः सङ्ख्ये नारायणकरच्युतैः । निपेतू राक्षसा भूमौ शैला वज्रहता इव ।। 7.7.14 ।।
transliteration: bhidyamānāḥ śaraiḥ saṅkhye nārāyaṇakaracyutaiḥ | nipetū rākṣasā bhūmau śailā vajrahatā iva || 7.7.14 ||
translation: भिद्यमानाः being pierced, शरैः by arrows, सङ्ख्ये in battle, नारायणकरच्युतैः released from Nārāyaṇa's hand, निपेतू fell, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, भूमौ on the ground, शैलाः mountains, वज्रहताः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like.
explanation: Being pierced by arrows released from Nārāyaṇa's hand in battle, the Rākṣasas fell to the ground like mountains struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: व्रणानि परगात्रेभ्यो विष्णुचक्रकृतानि वै । असृक्क्षरन्ति धाराभिः स्वर्णधारा इवाचलाः ।। 7.7.15 ।।
transliteration: vraṇāni paragātrebhyo viṣṇucakrakṛtāni vai | asṛkkṣaranti dhārābhiḥ svarṇadhārā ivācalāḥ || 7.7.15 ||
translation: व्रणानि wounds, परगात्रेभ्यः from the bodies of the enemies, विष्णुचक्रकृतानि made by Viṣṇu's discus, वै indeed, असृक् blood, क्षरन्ति flowed, धाराभिः in streams, स्वर्णधाराः streams of gold, इव like, अचलाः mountains.
explanation: From the enemies' bodies, wounds made by Viṣṇu's discus indeed streamed blood in torrents, resembling mountains from which streams of gold flow.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवश्चापि शार्ङ्गचापरस्वस्तथा । राक्षसानां रवांश्चापि ग्रसते वैष्णवो रवः ।। 7.7.16 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkharājaravaścāpi śārṅgacāparasvastathā | rākṣasānāṃ ravāṃścāpi grasate vaiṣṇavo ravaḥ || 7.7.16 ||
translation: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, च and, अपि also, शार्ङ्गचापरस्वः the twang of the Śārṅga bow, तथा similarly, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, रवान् sounds, च and, अपि also, ग्रसते devours, वैष्णवः the sound pertaining to Viṣṇu, रवः sound.
explanation: The sound of Viṣṇu's conch and the twang of his Śārṅga bow completely overpower and swallow the roars of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: तेषां शिरोधरान्धूताञ्छरध्वजधनूंषि च । रथान्पताकास्तूणीरांश्चिच्छेद स हरिः शरैः ।। 7.7.17 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ śirodharāndhūtāñcharadhvajadhanūṃṣi ca | rathānpatākāstūṇīrāṃściccheda sa hariḥ śaraiḥ || 7.7.17 ||
translation: तेषाम् their, शिरोधरान् necks, धूतान् severed, शरध्वजधनूंषि arrows, banners, and bows, च and, रथान् chariots, पताकाः flags, तूणीरान् quivers, चिच्छेद cut, सः he, हरिः Hari, शरैः with arrows.
explanation: Hari, with his arrows, severed their necks, and cut down their arrows, banners, bows, chariots, flags, and quivers.

shloka_text: सूर्यादिव करा घोरा ऊर्मयः सागरादिव । पर्वतादिव नागेन्द्रा धारौघा इव चाम्बुदात् ।। 7.7.18 ।।
transliteration: sūryādiva karā ghorā ūrmayaḥ sāgarādiva | parvatādiva nāgendrā dhāraughā iva cāmbudāt || 7.7.18 ||
translation: सूर्यात् from the sun, इव as if, कराः rays, घोराः terrible, ऊर्मयः waves, सागरात् from the ocean, इव as if, पर्वतात् from mountains, इव as if, नागेन्द्राः great elephants, धारौघाः torrents of rain, इव as if, च and, अम्बुदात् from a cloud.
explanation: Just as terrible rays emanate from the sun, waves from the ocean, great elephants from mountains, and torrents of rain from a cloud, so too did arrows emerge.

shloka_text: तथा शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः शरा नारायणेरिताः । निर्धावन्तीषवस्तूर्णं शतशोथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.19 ।।
transliteration: tathā śārṅgavinirmuktāḥ śarā nārāyaṇeritāḥ | nirdhāvantīṣavastūrṇaṃ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ || 7.7.19 ||
translation: तथा similarly, शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, शराः arrows, नारायणेरिताः propelled by Nārāyaṇa, निर्धावन्ति rushed forth, इषवः arrows, तूर्णं swiftly, शतशः by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: Similarly, arrows released from the Śārṅga bow and propelled by Nārāyaṇa rushed forth swiftly by hundreds and thousands.

shloka_text: शरभेण यथा सिंहाः सिंहेन द्विरदा यथा । द्विरदेन यथा व्याघ्रा व्याघ्रेण द्वीपिनो यथा ।। 7.7.20 ।।
transliteration: śarabheṇa yathā siṃhāḥ siṃhena dviradā yathā | dviradena yathā vyāghrā vyāghreṇa dvīpino yathā || 7.7.20 ||
translation: शरभेण by a Śarabha, यथा as, सिंहाः lions, सिंहेन by a lion, द्विरदाः elephants, यथा as, द्विरदेन by an elephant, यथा as, व्याघ्राः tigers, व्याघ्रेण by a tiger, द्वीपिनः leopards, यथा as.
explanation: Just as lions are overcome by a Śarabha, elephants by a lion, tigers by an elephant, and leopards by a tiger, so too were the Rākṣasas overwhelmed.

shloka_text: द्वीपिनेव यथा श्वानः शुना मार्जारका यथा । मार्जारेण यथा सर्पाः सर्पेण च यथा ऽ ऽखवः ।। 7.7.21 ।।
transliteration: dvīpineva yathā śvānaḥ śunā mārjārakā yathā | mārjāreṇa yathā sarpāḥ sarpeṇa ca yathā ' 'khavaḥ || 7.7.21 ||
translation: द्वीपिनेन by a leopard, इव as if, यथा just as, श्वानः dogs, शुना by a dog, मार्जारकाः cats, यथा just as, मार्जारेण by a cat, यथा just as, सर्पाः snakes, सर्पेण by a snake, च and, यथा just as, आखवः mice.
explanation: Just as dogs are afraid of a leopard, cats of a dog, snakes of a cat, and mice of a snake, so too were the rakshasas.

shloka_text: तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । द्रवन्ति द्राविताश्चन्ये शायिताश्च महीतले ।। 7.7.22 ।।
transliteration: tathā te rākṣasāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā | dravanti drāvitāścanye śāyitāśca mahītale || 7.7.22 ||
translation: तथा similarly, ते those, राक्षसाः rakshasas, सर्वे all, विष्णुना by Vishnu, प्रभविष्णुना by the all-powerful, द्रवन्ति flee, द्राविताः put to flight, च and, अन्ये others, शायिताः laid down, च and, महीतले on the ground.
explanation: Similarly, all those rakshasas fled from the all-powerful Vishnu, while others were put to flight or laid dead on the ground.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां सहस्राणि निहत्य मधुसूदनः । वारिजं पूरयामास तोयदं सुरराडिव ।। 7.7.23 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ sahasrāṇi nihatya madhusūdanaḥ | vārijaṃ pūrayāmāsa toyadaṃ surarāḍiva || 7.7.23 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of rakshasas, सहस्राणि thousands, निहत्य having killed, मधुसूदनः Madhusudana, वारिजम् the conch, पूरयामास he blew, तोयदम् a cloud, सुरराट् the king of gods, इव as if.
explanation: Having slain thousands of rakshasas, Madhusudana blew his conch, just as the king of gods (Indra) causes a cloud to thunder.

shloka_text: नारायणशरत्रस्तं शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् । ययौ लङ्कामभिमुखं प्रभग्नं राक्षसं बलम् ।। 7.7.24 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇaśaratrastaṃ śaṅkhanādasuvihvalam | yayau laṅkāmabhimukhaṃ prabhagnaṃ rākṣasaṃ balam || 7.7.24 ||
translation: नारायणशरत्रस्तम् terrified by Narayana's arrows, शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् greatly bewildered by the sound of the conch, ययौ went, लङ्काम् to Lanka, अभिमुखम् facing towards, प्रभग्नम् routed, राक्षसम् rakshasa, बलम् army.
explanation: The routed rakshasa army, terrified by Narayana's arrows and greatly bewildered by the sound of his conch, fled towards Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रभग्ने राक्षसबले नारायणशराहते । सुमाली शरवर्षेण निववार रणे हरिम् ।। 7.7.25 ।।
transliteration: prabhagne rākṣasabale nārāyaṇaśarāhate | sumālī śaravarṣeṇa nivavāra raṇe harim || 7.7.25 ||
translation: प्रभग्ने when routed, राक्षसबले the rakshasa army, नारायणशराहते struck by Narayana's arrows, सुमाली Sumali, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, निववार he obstructed, रणे in battle, हरिम् Hari.
explanation: When the rakshasa army was routed and struck by Narayana's arrows, Sumali, in battle, obstructed Hari with a shower of arrows.

shloka_text: स तु तं छादयामास नीहार इव भास्करम् । राक्षसाः सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः पुनर्धैर्यं समादधुः ।। 7.7.26 ।।
transliteration: sa tu taṃ chādayāmāsa nīhāra iva bhāskaram | rākṣasāḥ sattvasampannāḥ punardhairyaṃ samādadhuḥ || 7.7.26 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, तम् him, छादयामास covered, नीहारः mist, इव like, भास्करम् the sun. राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः endowed with strength, पुनः again, धैर्यम् courage, समादधुः regained.
explanation: He covered him like mist covers the sun, and the Rakshasas, filled with courage, regained their composure.

shloka_text: अथ सो ऽभ्यपतद्रोषाद्राक्षसो बलदर्पितः । महानादं प्रकुर्वाणो राक्षसाञ्जीवयन्निव ।। 7.7.27 ।।
transliteration: atha so 'bhyapatadroṣādrākṣaso baladarpitaḥ | mahānādaṃ prakurvāṇo rākṣasāñjīvayanniva || 7.7.27 ||
translation: अथ then, सः he, अभ्यपतत् rushed towards, रोषात् from anger, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, बलदर्पितः proud of his strength. महानादम् a great roar, प्रकुर्वाणः making, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, जीवयन् enlivening, इव as if.
explanation: Then, that Rakshasa, proud of his strength, rushed forward in anger, making a great roar as if to revive the other Rakshasas.

shloka_text: उत्क्षिप्य लम्बाभरणं धुन्वन्करमिव द्विपः । ररास राक्षसो हर्षात्सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.7.28 ।।
transliteration: utkṣipya lambābharaṇaṃ dhunvankaramiva dvipaḥ | rarāsa rākṣaso harṣātsataḍittoyado yathā || 7.7.28 ||
translation: उत्क्षिप्य lifting up, लम्बाभरणम् his long ornaments, धुन्वन् shaking, करम् his trunk, इव like, द्विपः an elephant. ररास roared, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, हर्षात् from joy, सतडित् with lightning, तोयदः a cloud, यथा just as.
explanation: Lifting his long ornaments and shaking them like an elephant shakes its trunk, the Rakshasa roared with joy, just like a thunderous cloud.

shloka_text: सुमालेर्नर्दतस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । चिच्छेद यन्तुरश्वाश्च भ्रान्तास्तस्य तु रक्षसः ।। 7.7.29 ।।
transliteration: sumālernardatastasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam | ciccheda yanturaśvāśca bhrāntāstasya tu rakṣasaḥ || 7.7.29 ||
translation: सुमालेः of Sumali, नर्दतः roaring, तस्य his, शिरः head, ज्वलितकुण्डलम् with shining earrings. चिच्छेद cut off, यन्तुः of the charioteer, अश्वाः horses, च and, भ्रान्ताः bewildered, तस्य his, तु indeed, रक्षसः of the Rakshasa.
explanation: (He) cut off the head of the roaring Sumali, which was adorned with shining earrings, and the horses of that Rakshasa's charioteer became bewildered.

shloka_text: तैरश्वैर्भ्राम्यते भ्रान्तैः सुमाली राक्षसेश्वरः । इन्द्रियाश्वैः परिभ्रान्तैर्धृतिहीनो यथा नरः ।। 7.7.30 ।।
transliteration: tairaśvairbhrāmyate bhrāntaiḥ sumālī rākṣaseśvaraḥ | indriyāśvaiḥ paribhrāntairdhṛtihīno yathā naraḥ || 7.7.30 ||
translation: तैः by those, अश्वैः horses, भ्रान्तैः bewildered, भ्राम्यते was whirled around, सुमाली Sumali, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas. इन्द्रियाश्वैः by the horses of senses, परिभ्रान्तैः bewildered, धृतिहीनः devoid of steadfastness, यथा just as, नरः a man.
explanation: Sumali, the lord of Rakshasas, was whirled around by those bewildered horses, just as a man devoid of steadfastness is bewildered by the horses of his senses.

shloka_text: ततो विष्णुं महाबाहुं प्रपतन्तं रणाजिरे । हृते सुमालेरश्वैश्च रथे विष्णुरथं प्रति ।। 7.7.31 ।।
transliteration: tato viṣṇuṃ mahābāhuṃ prapatantaṃ raṇājire | hṛte sumāleraśvaiśca rathe viṣṇurathaṃ prati || 7.7.31 ||
translation: ततः then, विष्णुम् Vishnu, महाबाहुम् the mighty-armed, प्रपतन्तम् falling down, रणाजिरे in the battlefield, हृते when taken away, सुमालेः by Sumali, अश्वैः by horses, च and, रथे the chariot, विष्णुरथम् Vishnu's chariot, प्रति towards
explanation: Then, as Vishnu's chariot was carried away by Sumali's horses, the mighty-armed Vishnu was seen falling down in the battlefield.

shloka_text: माली चाभ्यद्रवद्युक्तः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः । मालेर्धनुश्च्युता बाणाः कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः । विविशुर्हरिमासाद्य क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव ।। 7.7.32 ।।
transliteration: mālī cābhyadravadyuktaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ | mālerdhanuścyutā bāṇāḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitāḥ | viviśurharimāsādya krauñcaṃ patrarathā iva || 7.7.32 ||
translation: माली Mali, च and, अभ्यद्रवत् rushed towards, युक्तः ready, प्रगृह्य holding, सशरम् with arrows, धनुः bow, मालेः from Mali's, धनुः bow, च्युताः released, बाणाः arrows, कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः adorned with gold, विविशुः entered, हरिम् Vishnu, आसाद्य reaching, क्रौञ्चम् the Krauncha mountain, पत्ररथाः birds, इव like
explanation: Mali, ready and holding his bow with arrows, rushed towards Vishnu, and the gold-adorned arrows released from his bow pierced Vishnu, just as birds enter the Krauncha mountain.

shloka_text: अर्द्यमानः शरैः सो ऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः । चुक्षुभे न रणे विष्णुर्जितेन्द्रिय इवाधिभिः ।। 7.7.33 ।।
transliteration: ardyamānaḥ śaraiḥ so 'tha mālimuktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ | cukṣubhe na raṇe viṣṇurjitendriya ivādhibhiḥ || 7.7.33 ||
translation: अर्द्यमानः being tormented, शरैः by arrows, सः he (Vishnu), अथ then, मालिमुक्तैः released by Mali, सहस्रशः by thousands, चुक्षुभे न did not become agitated, रणे in battle, विष्णुः Vishnu, जितेन्द्रियः one who has controlled his senses, इव like, अधिभिः by mental anxieties
explanation: Though tormented by thousands of arrows released by Mali, Vishnu remained unagitated in battle, like a person who has controlled his senses is unaffected by mental anxieties.

shloka_text: अथ मौर्वीस्वनं कृत्वा भगवान्भूतभावनः । मालिनं प्रति बाणौघान्ससर्जारिनिषूदनः ।। 7.7.34 ।।
transliteration: atha maurvīsvanaṃ kṛtvā bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ | mālinaṃ prati bāṇaughānsasarjāriniṣūdanaḥ || 7.7.34 ||
translation: अथ then, मौर्वीस्वनम् the twang of the bowstring, कृत्वा making, भगवान् the divine one, भूतभावनः the creator of beings, मालिनम् Mali, प्रति towards, बाणौघान् showers of arrows, ससर्ज released, अरिनिषूदनः the destroyer of enemies
explanation: Then, the divine creator of beings and destroyer of enemies, making the twang of his bowstring, released showers of arrows towards Mali.

shloka_text: ते मालिदेहमासाद्य वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः शराः । पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव सुधारसम् ।। 7.7.35 ।।
transliteration: te mālidehamāsādya vajravidyutprabhāḥ śarāḥ | pibanti rudhiraṃ tasya nāgā iva sudhārasam || 7.7.35 ||
translation: ते those, मालिदेहम् Mali's body, आसाद्य reaching, वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः having the brilliance of thunderbolt and lightning, शराः arrows, पिबन्ति drank, रुधिरम् blood, तस्य his, नागाः serpents, इव like, सुधारसम् nectar
explanation: Those arrows, shining like thunderbolts and lightning, reached Mali's body and drank his blood as if serpents were drinking nectar.

shloka_text: मालिनं विमुखं कृत्वा शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः । मालिमौलिं ध्वजं चापं वाजिनश्चाप्यपातयत् ।। 7.7.36 ।।
transliteration: mālinaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ | mālimauliṃ dhvajaṃ cāpaṃ vājinaścāpyapātayat || 7.7.36 ||
translation: मालिनं Mali, विमुखं facing away, कृत्वा having made, शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः the one holding conch, discus, and mace, मालिमौलिं Mali's crown, ध्वजं banner, चापं bow, वाजिनः horses, च and, अपि also, अपातयत् struck down.
explanation: The wielder of the conch, discus, and mace turned Mali away and then struck down Mali's crown, banner, bow, and horses.

shloka_text: विरथस्तु गदां गृह्य माली नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः । आपुप्लुवे गदापाणिर्गिर्यग्रादिव केसरी ।। 7.7.37 ।।
transliteration: virathastu gadāṃ gṛhya mālī naktañcarottamaḥ | āpupluve gadāpāṇirgiryagrādiva kesarī || 7.7.37 ||
translation: विरथः chariot-less, तु but, गदां mace, गृह्य having taken, माली Mali, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः the best among night-wanderers, आपुप्लुवे sprang, गदापाणिः mace-in-hand, गिरि mountain, अग्रात् from the peak, इव like, केसरी a lion.
explanation: But Mali, the foremost among night-roaming demons, having lost his chariot, took up his mace and, mace in hand, sprang forward like a lion from a mountain peak.

shloka_text: गदया गरुडेशानमीशानमिव चान्तकः । ललाटदेशे ऽभ्यहनद्वज्रेणेन्द्रो यथा ऽचलम् ।। 7.7.38 ।।
transliteration: gadayā garuḍeśānamīśānamiva cāntakaḥ | lalāṭadeśe 'bhyahanadvajreṇendro yathā 'calam || 7.7.38 ||
translation: गदया with the mace, गरुडेशानं the lord of Garuda, ईशानं Shiva, इव like, च and, अन्तकः Yama, ललाटदेशे on the forehead region, अभ्यहनत् struck, वज्रेण with the thunderbolt, इन्द्रः Indra, यथा as, अचलम् a mountain.
explanation: With his mace, Mali struck the lord of Garuda on the forehead, just as Yama strikes Shiva, or as Indra strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: गदयाभिहतस्तेन मालिना गरुडो भृशम् । रणात्पराङ्मुखं देवं कृतवान्वेदनातुरः ।। 7.7.39 ।।
transliteration: gadayābhihatastena mālinā garuḍo bhṛśam | raṇātparāṅmukhaṃ devaṃ kṛtavānvedanāturaḥ || 7.7.39 ||
translation: गदया by the mace, अभिहतः struck, तेन by him, मालिना by Mali, गरुडः Garuda, भृशम् severely, रणात् from the battle, पराङ्मुखं facing away, देवं the god, कृतवान् made, वेदनातुरः distressed by pain.
explanation: Severely struck by Mali's mace, Garuda, distressed by the pain, caused the god (Vishnu) to turn away from the battle.

shloka_text: पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै । उदतिष्ठन्महाञ्छब्दो रक्षसामभिनर्दताम् ।। 7.7.40 ।।
transliteration: parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai | udatiṣṭhanmahāñchabdo rakṣasāmabhinardatām || 7.7.40 ||
translation: पराङ्मुखे facing away, कृते having been made, देवे the god, मालिना by Mali, गरुडेन by Garuda, वै indeed, उदतिष्ठत् arose, महान् great, शब्दः sound, रक्षसां of the demons, अभिनर्दताम् roaring.
explanation: When the god was indeed made to turn away by Mali (through Garuda), a great roaring sound arose from the exultant demons.

shloka_text: रक्षसां रवतां रावं श्रुत्वा हरिहयानुजः ।। 7.7.41 ।।
transliteration: rakṣasāṃ ravatāṃ rāvaṃ śrutvā harihayānujaḥ || 7.7.41 ||
translation: रक्षसां of the Rākṣasas, रवतां roaring, रावं sound, श्रुत्वा having heard, हरिहयानुजः the younger brother of Harihaya (Indra, i.e., Vishnu).
explanation: Having heard the roaring sound of the Rākṣasas, Vishnu, the younger brother of Indra, reacted.

shloka_text: तिर्यगास्थाय सङ्क्रुद्धः पक्षीशे भगवान्हरिः । पराङ्मुखो ऽप्युत्ससर्ज मालेश्चक्रं जिघांसया ।। 7.7.42 ।।
transliteration: tiryagāsthāya saṅkruddhaḥ pakṣīśe bhagavānhariḥ | parāṅmukho 'pyutsasarja māleścakraṃ jighāṃsayā || 7.7.42 ||
translation: तिर्यगास्थाय having stood obliquely, सङ्क्रुद्धः greatly enraged, पक्षीशे on the lord of birds (Garuda), भगवान् the divine, हरिः Hari (Vishnu), पराङ्मुखो ऽपि even though facing away, उत्ससर्ज released, मालेः at Māli, चक्रं the discus, जिघांसया with the desire to kill.
explanation: The divine Hari, greatly enraged, stood sideways on Garuda and, even while facing away, released his discus at Māli with the intention of killing him.

shloka_text: तत्सूर्यमण्डलाभासं स्वभासा भासयन्नभः । कालचक्रनिभं चक्रं मालेः शीर्षमपातयत् ।। 7.7.43 ।।
transliteration: tatsūryamaṇḍalābhāsaṃ svabhāsā bhāsayannabhaḥ | kālacakranibhaṃ cakraṃ māleḥ śīrṣamapātayat || 7.7.43 ||
translation: तत् that, सूर्यमण्डलाभासं resembling the orb of the sun, स्वभासा with its own radiance, भासयन् illuminating, नभः the sky, कालचक्रनिभं resembling the wheel of time, चक्रं discus, मालेः of Māli, शीर्षम् head, अपातयत् cut off.
explanation: That discus, resembling the sun's orb and illuminating the sky with its own brilliance, and appearing like the wheel of time, severed Māli's head.

shloka_text: तच्छिरो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रोत्कृत्तं बिभीषणम् । पपात रुधिरोद्गारि पुरा राहुशिरो यथा ।। 7.7.44 ।।
transliteration: tacchiro rākṣasendrasya cakrotkṛttaṃ bibhīṣaṇam | papāta rudhirodgāri purā rāhuśiro yathā || 7.7.44 ||
translation: तत् that, शिरो head, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of Rākṣasas, चक्रोत्कृत्तं severed by the discus, बिभीषणम् terrifying, पपात fell, रुधिरोद्गारि gushing blood, पुरा formerly, राहुशिरो Rāhu's head, यथा just as.
explanation: That terrifying head of the king of Rākṣasas, severed by the discus and gushing blood, fell just as Rāhu's head had fallen in ancient times.

shloka_text: ततः सुरैः संसहृष्टैः सर्वप्राणसमीरितः । सिंहनादरवोन्मुक्तः साधु देवेतिवादिभिः ।। 7.7.45 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ suraiḥ saṃsahṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaprāṇasamīritaḥ | siṃhanādaravonmuktaḥ sādhu devetivādibhiḥ || 7.7.45 ||
translation: ततः then, सुरैः by the gods, संसहृष्टैः greatly delighted, सर्वप्राणसमीरितः uttered with all their might, सिंहनादरवः a lion's roar (a mighty shout), उन्मुक्तः released, साधु देव "Well done, O God!", इतिवादिभिः those who said thus.
explanation: Then, the greatly delighted gods, exclaiming "Well done, O God!", uttered a mighty roar with all their might.

shloka_text: मालिनं निहतं दृष्ट्वा सुमाली माल्यवानपि । सबलौ शोकसन्तप्तौ लङ्कामेव प्रधावितौ ।। 7.7.46 ।।
transliteration: mālinaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā sumālī mālyavānapi | sabalau śokasantaptau laṅkāmeva pradhāvitau || 7.7.46 ||
translation: मालिनं Malina, निहतं slain, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सुमाली Sumali, माल्यवानपि and Malyavan also, सबलौ with their forces, शोकसन्तप्तौ tormented by grief, लङ्कामेव to Lanka itself, प्रधावितौ they fled
explanation: Seeing Malina slain, Sumali and Malyavan, along with their armies, were overcome with grief and fled back to Lanka.

shloka_text: गरुडस्तु समाश्वस्तः सन्निवृत्य यथा पुरा । राक्षसान्द्रावयामास पक्षवातेन कोपितः ।। 7.7.47 ।।
transliteration: garuḍastu samāśvastaḥ sannivṛtya yathā purā | rākṣasāndrāvayāmāsa pakṣavātena kopitaḥ || 7.7.47 ||
translation: गरुडस्तु but Garuda, समाश्वस्तः having recovered, सन्निवृत्य having returned, यथा as, पुरा before, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, द्रावयामास he made to flee, पक्षवातेन by the wind from his wings, कोपितः enraged
explanation: Garuda, having recovered and returned as before, angrily chased away the Rakshasas with the powerful wind generated by his wings.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमला गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः । लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवा मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः ।। 7.7.48 ।।
transliteration: cakrakṛttāsyakamalā gadāsañcūrṇitorasaḥ | lāṅgalaglapitagrīvā musalairbhinnamastakāḥ || 7.7.48 ||
translation: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलाः whose lotus-like faces were severed by the discus, गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः whose chests were crushed by maces, लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवाः whose necks were destroyed by ploughs, मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः whose heads were shattered by pestles
explanation: The Rakshasas had their lotus-like faces severed by the discus, their chests crushed by maces, their necks destroyed by ploughs, and their heads shattered by pestles.

shloka_text: केचिच्चैवासिना छिन्नास्तथान्ये शरपीडिताः । निपेतुरम्बरात्तूर्णं राक्षसाः सागराम्भसि ।। 7.7.49 ।।
transliteration: keciccaivāsinā chinnāstathānye śarapīḍitāḥ | nipeturambarāttūrṇaṃ rākṣasāḥ sāgarāmbhasi || 7.7.49 ||
translation: केचित् some, चैव and indeed, असिना by swords, छिन्नाः cut, तथान्ये similarly others, शरपीडिताः tormented by arrows, निपेतुरम्बरात् fell from the sky, तूर्णं quickly, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सागराम्भसि into the ocean's waters
explanation: Some Rakshasas were cut down by swords, others were wounded by arrows, and all of them swiftly fell from the sky into the ocean's waters.

shloka_text: नारायणो बाणवराशनीभिर्विदारयामास धनुर्विमुक्तैः । नक्तञ्चरान्मुक्तविधूतकेशान्यथा ऽशनीभिः सतडिन्महाभ्राः ।। 7.7.50 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇo bāṇavarāśanībhirvidārayāmāsa dhanurvimuktaiḥ | naktañcarānmuktavidhūtakeśānyathā 'śanībhiḥ sataḍinmahābhrāḥ || 7.7.50 ||
translation: नारायणो Narayana, बाणवराशनीभिः with excellent arrows like thunderbolts, विदारयामास tore apart, धनुर्विमुक्तैः released from his bow, नक्तञ्चरान् the night-wanderers (Rakshasas), मुक्तविधूतकेशान् whose hair was loose and disheveled, यथा just as, अशनीभिः by thunderbolts, सतडिन्महाभ्राः great clouds with lightning
explanation: Narayana, with excellent arrows released from his bow like thunderbolts, tore apart the night-wandering Rakshasas whose hair was loose and disheveled, just as thunderbolts tear apart great clouds accompanied by lightning.

shloka_text: भिन्नातपत्रं पतमानमस्त्रं शरैरपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् । विनिस्सृतान्त्रं भयलोलनेत्रं बलं तदुन्मत्ततरं बभूव ।। 7.7.51 ।।
transliteration: bhinnātapatraṃ patamānamastraṃ śarairapadhvastavinītaveṣam | vinissṛtāntraṃ bhayalolanetraṃ balaṃ tadunmattataraṃ babhūva || 7.7.51 ||
translation: भिन्नातपत्रं with broken umbrellas, पतमानमस्त्रं with falling weapons, शरैः by arrows, अपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् with proper attire destroyed, विनिस्सृतान्त्रं with intestines gushing out, भयलोलनेत्रं with eyes rolling in fear, बलं the army, तत् that, उन्मत्ततरं more maddened, बभूव became
explanation: The army became utterly frenzied, with their royal canopies shattered, weapons dropping, proper attire torn by arrows, intestines spilling out, and eyes wide with terror.

shloka_text: सिंहार्दितानामिव कुञ्जराणां निशाचराणां सह कुञ्जराणाम् । रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम् ।। 7.7.52 ।।
transliteration: siṃhārditānāmiva kuñjarāṇāṃ niśācarāṇāṃ saha kuñjarāṇām | ravāśca vegāśca samaṃ babhūvuḥ purāṇasiṃhena vimarditānām || 7.7.52 ||
translation: सिंहार्दितानाम् of those tormented by a lion, इव like, कुञ्जराणां of elephants, निशाचराणां of night-rovers (Rakshasas), सह with, कुञ्जराणाम् of elephants, रवाः roars/cries, च and, वेगाः speeds/rushes, च and, समं together/simultaneously, बभूवुः became/occurred, पुराणसिंहेन by the ancient lion, विमर्दितानाम् of those crushed
explanation: The roars and frantic movements of the Rakshasas and their elephants, tormented by the ancient lion, were like those of elephants distressed by a lion.

shloka_text: ते वार्यमाणा हरिबाणजालैः सबाणजालानि समुत्सृजन्तः । धावन्ति नक्तञ्चरकालमेघा वायुप्रभिन्ना इव कालमेघाः ।। 7.7.53 ।।
transliteration: te vāryamāṇā haribāṇajālaiḥ sabāṇajālāni samutsṛjantaḥ | dhāvanti naktañcarakālameghā vāyuprabhinnā iva kālameghāḥ || 7.7.53 ||
translation: ते they, वार्यमाणाः being obstructed/repelled, हरिबाणजालैः by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, सबाणजालानि their own showers of arrows, समुत्सृजन्तः abandoning/throwing away, धावन्ति run, नक्तञ्चरकालमेघाः the Rakshasas, like dark clouds, वायुप्रभिन्नाः scattered by the wind, इव like, कालमेघाः dark clouds
explanation: Those Rakshasas, like dark clouds, were repelled by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, and abandoning their own arrows, they fled like storm clouds scattered by the wind.

shloka_text: चक्रपहारैर्विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाश्च गदाप्रहारैः । अभिप्रहारैर्द्विविधा विभिन्नाः पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः ।। 7.7.54 ।।
transliteration: cakrapahārairvinikṛttaśīrṣāḥ sañcūrṇitāṅgāśca gadāprahāraiḥ | abhiprahārairdvividhā vibhinnāḥ patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ || 7.7.54 ||
translation: चक्रपहारैः by blows of discus, विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः with severed heads, सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाः with crushed limbs, च and, गदाप्रहारैः by blows of mace, अभिप्रहारैः by various attacks, द्विविधाः in two ways/halves, विभिन्नाः split/torn apart, पतन्ति fall, शैलाः mountains, इव like, राक्षसेन्द्राः Rakshasa lords/chiefs
explanation: The chief Rakshasas, with their heads severed by discus blows, limbs crushed by mace blows, and bodies split in two by various attacks, fell like mountains.

shloka_text: विलम्बमानैर्मणिहारकुण्डलैर्निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः । निपात्यमानैर्ददृशे निरन्तरं निपात्यमानैरिव नीलपर्वतैः ।। 7.7.55 ।।
transliteration: vilambamānairmaṇihārakuṇḍalairniśācarairnīlabalāhakopamaiḥ | nipātyamānairdadṛśe nirantaraṃ nipātyamānairiva nīlaparvataiḥ || 7.7.55 ||
translation: विलम्बमानैः hanging down, मणिहारकुण्डलैः with jewel necklaces and earrings, निशाचरैः by the night-rovers (Rakshasas), नीलबलाहकोपमैः resembling blue clouds, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, ददृशे was seen, निरन्तरं continuously/without gap, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, इव like, नीलपर्वतैः by blue mountains
explanation: The falling Rakshasas, who resembled dark blue clouds and wore dangling jewel necklaces and earrings, were continuously seen falling like blue mountains being struck down. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः ।। 7 ।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
